analysis.title: Flows & Liquidity: Equity vulnerabilities
key_insights: Elevated equity positioning and leverage have re-emerged, to a lesser extent than last June/July, which JPM says poses some challenge to equities into Q4. At the end of July, JPM had noted that earlier excesses had largely unwound.
Leverage via US equity futures held by asset managers and leveraged funds has rebounded and is close to YTD highs.
JPM's broad equity positioning indicator appears to have peaked in September, after earlier peaks in January 2026 and August 2025.

Short interest in SPY appears to be bottoming after a record low at the start of September. Short interest in semiconductor ETFs SMH and DRAM has normalized, which suggests short covering is largely behind us.

Momentum signals in tech-heavy indices (Nasdaq, Kospi, Taiwan, Nikkei) have rebounded, so CTAs have begun rebuilding long positions, though far from previous extremes. The April-June relative trade of selling HSCEI and buying Korea and Taiwan re-emerged in August-September.

The AUM of leveraged equity ETFs relative to the market cap of underlying stocks has risen in recent weeks across all leveraged equity ETFs, to about 70% of the way between its April low and June high. For memory stocks the ratio is about 50% of its April-June range. JPM warns the leveraged ETF problem could re-emerge as a source of deleveraging and excess volatility if the increase continues.

NYSE margin account net debit balances (a proxy for US individual investor leverage) stayed very elevated in August and barely changed after the June/July deleveraging, which JPM calls a significant vulnerability for equities.

JPM still sees the tech/AI complex supported fundamentally, so a renewed equity VaR shock like June/July would not derail the tech bull market. Support comes from rising memory prices, higher hyperscaler capex projections and holding AI compute prices.

Consensus hyperscaler capex projections rose to $805bn for 2026 and $1.1tr for 2027, from $758bn and $925bn on July 1st. Bloomberg consensus shows 2026E total $804.9bn (+113% y/y) and 2027E $1,091.8bn (+36%).

Hopper GPU rental prices show some improvement in recent months after downward pressure into end-2025, which JPM says casts doubt on excessive obsolescence/depreciation assumptions made by some investors.

Global bond fund inflows are tracking an annualized pace of about $1.7tr, above the roughly $1.1tr implied by JPM's forecasting model. Adding contemporaneous equity returns implies about $1.4tr, so strong equity returns explain about half of the gap, likely through retail rebalancing.

Bond fund inflows have had little effect on capping yields because the duration impulse is weak. Duration-adjusted inflow runs at about half the unadjusted pace, equal to about $0.9tr in Global Agg duration terms. The duration impulse shifted from positive in 2023-24 to negative in 2025-26 YTD.

JPM's bond market reaction metric shows bond investors have become increasingly long duration versus what they wanted as markets repriced central bank policy expectations, after being neutral in late August. The cross-asset positioning metric also shows bond positions on the long side.

The dollar rally over the past month pushed DXY above 100 and EURUSD below 1.14. Spec and CTA positioning are short the euro and long the dollar, yet JPM sees the euro trading long, a gap it attributes to corporate hedging.

Corporate hedging proxies suggest euro corporates went effectively long the euro and US corporates went short the dollar before the dollar rally. JPM suggests hedgers may be normalizing, adding downward pressure on the euro and upward pressure on the dollar. Proxies lag, so confirmation would take at least a few weeks.

Cross-asset volatility monitor as of 28 Sep 2026: S&P 500 3m implied vol 14% (at its 1-year low of 14%, set 3 Sep), 10y US swaps vol 99% (at the 1-year high set 28 Sep), Brent 51%, CDX IG 42% with implied/realized of 2.14x.
Bitcoin market price of $83k is slightly below the estimated production cost of $85k. CME Bitcoin trading volume is down 35% y/y and CME Ethereum is down 17%.
2026 YTD performance to 29 Sep: CTAs +9.4%, Equity L/S +8.3%, Macro ex-CTAs +6.1%, Risk Parity +5.9%, MSCI AC World +13.1%, Barclays Global Agg -1.4%.

sector_views.rationale: JPM sees the tech/AI complex supported fundamentally by rising memory prices, higher hyperscaler capex projections and holding compute rental prices, despite positioning headwinds.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Dollar rallied over the past month. Spec and CTA positioning are long the dollar, while corporate hedging adjustments may add further support.
Euro weakened over the past month. Spec positioning is short, but JPM says the euro is trading long because of earlier corporate hedging.
Above the $1.1tr implied by JPM's forecasting model, but with little effect on yields because of a weak duration impulse.
Raised from $758bn and $925bn on July 1st, supporting the tech/AI complex.
Market price of $83k sits just below estimated production cost.

crypto_views: Bitcoin market price of $83k is just below the production cost estimate of $85k, based on the Hayes (2018) cost-of-production approach.
CME Bitcoin trading volume is down 35% y/y and CME Ethereum volume is down 17% y/y as of August 2026.
risk_factors: Re-emerged equity positioning and leverage could be a headwind for equities into Q4.
Leveraged equity ETFs could cause deleveraging and excess volatility if their AUM grows further.
Elevated margin account leverage among US individual investors is a significant vulnerability.
A renewed equity VaR shock like June/July is possible, though JPM does not expect it to derail the tech bull market.
Weak duration impulse from bond fund inflows provides less support for bond yields.
Corporate hedging normalization could pressure the euro further and lift the dollar.

tension_points.bull_case: Memory prices are still rising, hyperscaler capex projections were raised to $805bn for 2026 and $1.1tr for 2027, and Hopper GPU rental prices are holding up, so the tech/AI bull market would survive a renewed VaR shock.
tension_points.bear_case: Equity positioning and leverage have re-emerged, with futures leverage near YTD highs, rising leveraged ETF AUM and very elevated margin debt, a headwind for equities into Q4.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further increases in leveraged equity ETF AUM, which JPM says could re-emerge as a cause of deleveraging and excess volatility.
